skill.description: Scaffold Better Auth for TypeScript and JavaScript applications with framework detection, database adapters, OAuth providers, route handlers, plugins, and authentication pages.
skill.summary: Plan and implement Better Auth authentication for new, existing, or migrating web applications.

security_audit.summary: Contextual review confirmed five findings because the skill directs package installation and database migration commands. Other matches are documentation syntax, links, configuration examples, or standard environment access. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Migration commands execute an unpinned CLI package through the latest tag.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed Better Auth CLI version and use the project package manager lockfile before running generation or migration commands.

remediation.issue: Installation and migration commands can change dependencies, generated files, and database state.
remediation.suggestion: Request command-specific approval, show expected changes, and require database backups before applying production migrations.

content.value_statement: Authentication setup requires coordinated framework, database, provider, route, and interface changes. This skill plans and implements a Better Auth integration for your application.
actual_capabilities: Detects supported frameworks, package managers, databases, ORMs, and existing authentication libraries.
Collects authentication methods, providers, plugins, email requirements, and interface preferences.
Creates Better Auth server, client, route handler, and environment configuration.
Configures Prisma, Drizzle, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQLite database integrations.
Adds OAuth, email authentication, two-factor authentication, organizations, passkeys, and related plugins.
Builds authentication pages and provides migration, deployment, testing, and security guidance.
limitations: Supports TypeScript and JavaScript applications that can use Better Auth.
Requires users to provide database access, OAuth credentials, email services, and deployment settings.
Database migrations and package installation can change project and database state.
Generated interfaces may require adjustment for existing design systems and accessibility requirements.

use_cases.title: Launch Authentication
use_cases.description: Create sign-in, sign-up, session, route, database, and provider integration for a new web application.
use_cases.target_user: Application developers starting a TypeScript project

use_cases.title: Add Auth to an Existing App
use_cases.description: Inspect the current architecture and integrate Better Auth without replacing unrelated application structure.
use_cases.target_user: Teams extending an established JavaScript application

use_cases.title: Migrate Authentication
use_cases.description: Plan an incremental transition from another authentication library while preserving routes, sessions, and user flows.
use_cases.target_user: Technical leads managing an authentication migration

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Add Better Auth to this project with email and password sign-in. Inspect the framework and database, then ask for missing requirements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a project without authentication

prompt_templates.title: Add Social Providers
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure Better Auth with Google and GitHub OAuth. Include callback routes, required environment variables, sign-in pages, and provider setup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate Existing Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the current authentication implementation and plan a staged Better Auth migration. Preserve active sessions where feasible and identify compatibility risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration from another authentication library

prompt_templates.title: Build Enterprise Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement Better Auth with organizations, two-factor authentication, passkeys, email verification, rate limits, and production migrations. Review every security-sensitive configuration.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced authentication for a sensitive application

output_examples.input: Add email authentication to my Next.js application using Prisma and PostgreSQL.
output: A confirmed implementation plan covering routes, database changes, environment settings, and interface pages.
Better Auth server and client integration aligned with the existing Next.js structure.
Prisma schema generation, migration guidance, and a production security checklist.

output_examples.input: Add Google OAuth and organization support to an existing SvelteKit application.
output: A project assessment that preserves the current database and package manager.
SvelteKit handlers, Google provider configuration, organization plugins, and matching client integration.
Credential, callback, migration, testing, and deployment steps.

output_examples.input: Plan a migration from another authentication library.
output_examples.output: A staged migration plan covering current behavior, route replacement, session compatibility, user data, rollback points, and removal of the previous library.

best_practices: Confirm the implementation plan before changing dependencies, files, or database schemas.
Store secrets in environment variables and configure secure cookies, trusted origins, verification, and rate limits.
Pin package versions, review generated migrations, and back up production databases before applying changes.
anti_patterns: Do not disable CSRF protection or weaken cookie security to resolve configuration errors.
Do not embed database URLs, authentication secrets, or OAuth credentials in source files.
Do not run development schema push commands against production databases.

faq.question: Which frameworks are supported?
faq.answer: The guidance covers Next.js, SvelteKit, Nuxt, Astro, Express, Hono, SolidStart, and compatible JavaScript applications.

faq.question: Which databases can I use?
faq.answer: It covers PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, and MongoDB through supported drivers or Prisma, Drizzle, and MongoDB adapters.

faq.question: Can it add social sign-in?
faq.answer: Yes. It can configure providers such as Google, GitHub, Apple, Microsoft, Discord, and Twitter with required credentials.

faq.question: Does it create authentication pages?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create sign-in, sign-up, password recovery, reset, and email verification pages based on selected methods.

faq.question: Will it run database migrations?
faq.answer: It provides adapter-specific commands and may run them after approval. Review generated migrations and back up production data first.

faq.question: Does it replace security review?
faq.answer: No. Review authorization rules, account linking, secrets, cookies, origins, rate limits, email flows, and deployment settings before release.
